patch.value: Scope the json renderer to the commands this extension owns so it stops colliding with sibling extensions

The json renderer was registered through the unscoped defineRendererOverride overload, so the host treated it as owning every command. Two consequences: it was the last remaining extension_renderer_collision in the 17-package fleet union (against pm-context, which declares ownership correctly), and an unscoped renderer is one guard-bug away from replacing all pm --json output. The SDK exposes a scoped overload taking ScopedRendererOverrideDefinition {commands?, resultDiscriminator?, run}, and the declarative renderers map accepts it, so ownership can be declared without leaving the blueprint style this package demonstrates. Deliberately excludes list: this extension overrides the list command, but that override returns ctx.result untouched, so list never produces a payload the renderer should reshape.

The json renderer declares a non-empty commands list plus a resultDiscriminator; the renderer declines a command it does not own even when handed this extension's own payload; list is not in the owned set; pm health on the fleet union reports zero extension_renderer_collision warnings; all tests pass and typecheck is clean.

value.author: harness:claude-code
value.text:
VERIFIED IN THE REAL UNION, not just in tests.

Method: installed the 17 published fleet packages into a clean scratch workspace on pm-cli 2026.8.5, then swapped this package's freshly built dist into the installed extension directory and re-ran pm health.

Measured progression of total extension warnings in that union:
- 20 on pm-cli 2026.8.3 (9 of them renderer collisions)
- 12 on 2026.8.5, after upstream PR 893 taught the collision check to suppress statically disjoint ownership (renderer collisions 9 -> 1; the 1 was this package)
- 11 with this change: extension_renderer_collision no longer appears at all

Confirmed disjoint from every sibling that declares ownership: pm-starter owns ['starter demo'], pm-context owns ['context-pack','context-handoff','context-usage'], pm-changelog owns ['changelog generate','changelog export'], pm-ops owns OPS_COMMAND_PATHS. This package's owned set is 'hello' plus the ts-starter and ts-starter-demo paths, which intersects none of them.

The SDK test harness ENFORCES the ownership list, which is how the pre-existing renderer test caught it: that test passed command 'ts-starter-demo', which is not a real command path (the real ones are 'ts-starter-demo import' and 'ts-starter-demo export'), so once ownership was declared the renderer correctly declined and the assertion failed. Corrected the test to a real owned path rather than widening ownership to match the test.
